display.title: Simchas Beis Hashoeva Rally, Hoshana Rabbah Night: Dancing That Broke a Decree
display.summary_short: A live children's rally on the night of Hoshana Rabbah: the Twelve Pesukim, dancing with the Ushpizin, and a Chassid of the Tzemach Tzedek whose joy saved his sick son.
display.summary_long: A live Simchas Beis Hashoeva rally on the seventh night of Sukkos, Hoshana Rabbah. The host introduces the night's Ushpizin, Dovid HaMelech and the Rebbe Rashab, who both work to bring Moshiach, and children come up to recite the Twelve Pesukim, ending with 'We want Moshiach now'. With Simcha Engel the puppet, the host explains Hoshana Rabbah, the sweet apple in honey, and how all the Ushpizin come every night with one leading; as the Rebbe taught, when you take another Jew's hand and dance, you are dancing with Moshiach. He reminds the children of the Rebbe's request that each child have his own siddur, Chumash and tzedakah box. Then a story: a Chassid of the Tzemach Tzedek travels for days to the Rebbe on Hoshana Rabbah because his son is gravely ill, and receives a blessing that does not sound like a promise. He says Tehillim all day in tears, but at night, when everyone dances hakafos, he decides Hashem wants him to dance, and dances through Shemini Atzeres and Simchas Torah. The Tzemach Tzedek then tells him his joy broke the decree, and he finds his son healthy at home. The rally closes with 'I Believe in Hashem'.
display.lesson: Joy breaks every decree; dance with all your strength, even when you do not feel like it, to bring the Geulah.

date.note: 'Tav Shin Pei Hei', 'tonight is the seventh day of Sukkos' and 'tonight it's Hoshana Rabbah': evening of 22 Oct 2024.

advisories.note: A boy is gravely ill and the doctors cannot help; he recovers.

sources_cited.note: The Ushpizin join the Simchas Beis Hashoeva, and taking another Jew's hand to dance is dancing with Moshiach.
'Write me good news and you will not need to write about problems.'
Today Tehillim with simcha works better than with tears; make your feet dance even when you do not feel like it.
Each child should have his own siddur, Chumash and tzedakah box (Mikdash Me'at).
